result:
I found 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings or the module docstring's common rules, and fixed all of them. There are 150 rules in total. I checked them all by building a reference implementation straight from each docstring and comparing results over boundary values (threshold −1, threshold, threshold +1 and so on) and a range of unit prices. Before the fix, 10 rules gave different results; after it, all 150 match.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 25, 77 | The cap was applied to the amount before the discount, not to the discount itself | Cap the discount amount |
| 117 | Same problem: the price was capped (`min(base, 30000)`), not the discount | Cap the discount amount |
| 45 | The cap only kicked in once the discount passed 200,000, so discounts between 100,000 and 200,000 weren't capped | Always cap at 100,000 |
| 49, 89, 147 | Used `round()`, which rounds instead of flooring to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 76 | Discount started at 51 units (`qty >= 51`), not 50 | `qty >= 50` |
| 92, 134 | `qty > N` left out the threshold itself | `qty >= N` |

The other forms (`N <= qty`, `not qty < N`, `if disc > N: disc = N`, and so on) are written differently but behave the same, so I left them as they were. A copy of the original is saved at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
